onboarding.message:
Welcome to the {project} crew. You are {agent}{persona}.
At the end of every turn, set your own speech bubble: one short sentence in {language}, at most 80 characters, about what you are doing or just finished, no secrets:
herdr pane report-metadata "$HERDR_PANE_ID" --source crew --token say="<text>"
Messages from {lead} start with {prefix}, messages from other agents with [agent-name].
onboarding.ask: these agents are new to the crew. Please onboard them following the herdr-crew skill: give the ones without a persona a name, pronouns and role, register it with the command shown, and pass on the crew conventions (own bubble, prefixes).
panels.head: From the crew dashboard: the user asks for a new panel. The request, as plain text:
panels.make: Turn it into one panel of a built-in type, following the Panels section of the herdr-crew skill. No HTML or code of your own. Types:
panels.add: Add it with the command below; the dashboard shows it within a few seconds, without a restart. For example:
panels.end: Then tell the user which panel you added. If no type fits, explain that instead of building something else.
widget.remove: Removes the panel {title} ({id}) from .herdr-crew.json. Processes the panel started keep running.

summary.system: You write the speech bubble of the orchestrator on a dashboard of AI agents. Summarise in two short paragraphs separated by a blank line (at most 100 words together). First: what just happened, was decided or finished. Second: who works on what now and what comes next. First person, concrete, without numbers, paths or code. No quotes, no dashes, no emoji. Return only the text.
ui.languageAddHint: {name} translates the dashboard texts into this language and adds it to this project; the server translates nothing itself. You see the message before it is sent.
ui.languageNoLead: There is no lead persona in .herdr-crew.json (lead: true), so nobody can add the language.
ui.languageSent: Sent to {name}. The language shows up in this list once it is added.
languages.head: From the crew dashboard: the user asks for a new dashboard language. The language, as plain text:
languages.translate: Translate {en} into that language and write the result to {draft}: one JSON object with exactly the same keys, following the Languages section of the herdr-crew skill.
languages.rules: Translate faithfully. Keep every placeholder such as {name} unchanged, keep commands, file names and config keys such as .herdr-crew.json as they are, and keep confirmation and safety texts literal and complete: they explain what an action does. Set meta.name to the name of the language in that language and meta.englishName to its English name.
languages.commands: Check the file, then add it with a short lowercase language code such as de:
languages.end: Then tell the user that the language can be chosen with the 🌐 button. If the check reports problems, fix the file and run the check again.
